summary.text: A 48-year-old woman was referred for elective total thyroidectomy for bilateral multinodular goiter with progressive growth over two years and mild anterior cervical compression. She was euthyroid without severe dyspnea or dysphagia, had an unremarkable history, and examination showed thyroid enlargement more prominent on the right, no palpable lymphadenopathy and normal phonation.

Cervical ultrasound showed multiple bilateral nodules, the largest in the right lobe, without suspicious lymph nodes. Preoperative cervicothoracic CT demonstrated an aberrant right subclavian artery with a retroesophageal course, consistent with an arteria lusoria, with absence of the brachiocephalic trunk.

Total thyroidectomy was done under general anesthesia with neuromonitoring, dissecting the left side first with the RLN and parathyroid glands preserved. On the right, the RLN was not found in the tracheoesophageal groove, an NRLN was suspected, and a nerve branch arising directly from the cervical vagus was identified; proximal vagal stimulation gave a positive motor response and the NRLN was preserved without complications.
Recovery was uneventful with no voice changes or signs of hypocalcemia, no additional postoperative imaging was required, and the patient was discharged on the second postoperative day.

article_limitations: Discussion and introduction paragraphs are general or literature statements and are not recorded as patient facts, except the in-case statement in b00022 ("In the present case") that nerve function was preserved.

The abstract describes IONM confirming functional integrity of the nerve; the case text gives a positive motor response to proximal vagus stimulation. They describe the single intraoperative IONM confirmation and are recorded as one result citing both.
Figure 1 and Figure 2 caption sentences about the index patient's CT and operative photograph are recorded as caption-text observations; no values were read from pixels.
No dates, durations of surgery or laboratory values are given for the patient; thyroid status is stated only as euthyroid.
